_comment: CAPABILITY suite for the PostgreSQL CDC stream source with initial_load UNDER LIVE CHANGES, over every table of the employees model and its xp_sentinel (functions/caps_postgrescdc_initial_load.py::postgrescdc_initial_load_live). STAGES, in order: (1) domains -- create the postgrescdc domain, install the employees model, load the xs seed; (2) live -- `tdd domain sentinel-data --key after-create-data` (one xp_sentinel row stamped after the seed, so the snapshot carries it), then start `churn` in the background: 20 passes back to back, `tdd domain modify-data --ops Mix --sets 5` (employees insert/update/delete, departments update; a deleted employee cascades to dept_emp, dept_manager, titles and salaries); it keeps running through the stages below; (3) collections -- the project and one postgres_cdc source collection; (4) functions -- register the @stream_publisher, which STARTS it: its initial_load snapshot is taken over tables changing under it, and every change after the snapshot's position arrives as a CDC row, none missed; over the domain's own replication slot (replication_slot_behavior=reuse) the snapshot is a transaction of its own, so a change committing as it is taken may arrive twice; (5) live -- wait for churn to finish, then `sentinel-data --key after-churn`, written after the last change; (6) sentinel -- hold until both keys are in versions of xp_sentinel_changes (at most 5m each): after-churn arriving means every change before it has flushed; (7) monitor. The run takes ~1.5 min. With a pause between passes (a `pause` of 30s) each flush carries one pass and the stream falls behind -- after-churn then lands minutes late. The slot pins WAL until the domain is destroyed, which drops it. Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite container-connectors/postgrescdc_initial_load_live --keep`.
